meta.purpose: Labelled claims with KNOWN truth, used to measure the independent verifier and to decide whether a cheap model earns the right to replace the predecessor verification technique.
meta.labelling_rule: label=TRUE means the claim is correct AND scoped to its evidence. label=FALSE means the claim is wrong or wider than its evidence, even when the underlying observation was true.
meta.growth_target: ~50 claims, harvested from .claude/plans history.jsonl and reasoning traces. This file is the seed (10) required by FEAT-E, not the target.
meta.seed_note: FEAT-E also named a '453 rewritten refs' claim as a TRUE seed. It was NOT included: it could not be re-measured at corpus-build time, and an unverifiable TRUE label would poison the only thing this corpus is for. rules/core/no-assumption.md.

cove_decision.measurement_note: The deterministic-gate arm is re-measured on every run by `node aura-frog/scripts/verifier-corpus-eval.cjs` — the numbers deliberately live in the script, not here, so this record cannot go stale. The two model arms (cheap-model recall over FALSE claims, and agreement rate with FALSE claims, versus the predecessor technique) require live model calls and are NOT measured yet; `measurement: null` is what blocks the deletion.
deletion_conditions: cheap-model recall over FALSE claims strictly greater than the predecessor's
cheap-model agreement rate with FALSE claims strictly lower than the predecessor's
zero-reference proof: 0 referencing files, full-name match, population from git ls-files

claims.label: FALSE
claims.claim: claude -p does not accept slash commands
claims.observation: ran claude -p "/run" and it printed: Error: Reached max turns (1)
claims.real_cause: Print mode does accept user-invoked commands. Two separate mistakes stacked: the command name does not exist in that namespace (/run vs /aura-frog:run), and --max-turns 1 prints 'Error: Reached max turns', which reads like a command failure and is not.
claims.provenance: the motivating failure recorded in FEAT-E; ground truth re-probed 2026-10-29 (/aura-frog:run executed in print mode)

claims.label: FALSE
claims.claim: jest function coverage can never reach the 40% floor in this repo
claims.real_cause: Unreachable BY WRITING TESTS ALONE, not unreachable: 24 of the hooks execute main() on require and export nothing, so ~18% of the function scope is untestable until the hook-runtime refactor makes them importable. 'Never' is wider than the evidence.

claims.label: FALSE
claims.claim: the next-counter test is flaky because jest is broken
claims.observation: the test timed out after 5s on macOS while two workers held the counter
claims.real_cause: Missing mutual exclusion around the counter, not a defect in the runner. Fixed with file locking; 784/784 passed afterwards.
claims.provenance: project memory, CI-state note on this branch
